**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject duplicate force identities within a batch**

When one batch contains two force samples for the same undirected node pair, field profile, and embedding model—including reversed endpoints—both rows become updates for the same unique identity. Because the bulk write is unordered, conflicting similarities or charges can leave a nondeterministic final force sample. Track the canonical force tuple during this preflight and reject duplicates before `bulkWrite`, as is already done for semantic edges.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate force embedding dimensions before writing**

A JavaScript caller can supply `embedding_dimensions` as `NaN`, a fractional/negative number, or even a string, and this value is written directly despite `GraphSemanticForceSampleDocument` requiring `number | null`. Such rows corrupt the model/dimension metadata used to interpret force samples; validate a supplied value as a positive safe integer before any batch write.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

+(ns openplanner.graph.claims.boundary
+  "JavaScript/CLJS conversion boundary for edge-claim logic.
+
+  All JS object field aliases, Date parsing, number coercion, JSON canonicalizing,
+  and Node crypto calls live here. The pure core namespace receives normalized
+  CLJS maps only."
+  (:require [clojure.string :as str]
+            [goog.crypt :as crypt]
+            [openplanner.graph.claims.core :as claims]
+            [openplanner.graph.claims.policy :as policy]
+            [openplanner.graph.claims.schema :as schema])
+  (:import [goog.crypt Sha256]))
+
+(defn- js-object?
+  [value]
+  (and (some? value)
+       (= "object" (goog/typeOf value))
+       (not (array? value))))
+
+(defn- jget
+  [obj k]
+  (when (js-object? obj)
+    (aget obj k)))
+
+(defn- nonblank
+  [value]
+  (when (string? value)
+    (let [s (str/trim value)]
+      (when-not (str/blank? s) s))))
+
+(defn- agreeing-alias
+  "Every explicitly supplied identity alias must be a matching nonblank string."
+  [input fields fallback]
+  (let [supplied (when (js-object? input)
+                   (filter #(js/Object.hasOwn input %) fields))
+        values (map #(nonblank (jget input %)) supplied)]
+    (if (seq supplied)
+      (when (and (every? some? values) (= 1 (count (set values)))) (first values))
+      fallback)))
+
+(defn- token-keyword
+  [value]
+  (some-> value str str/trim str/lower-case (str/replace #"-" "_") keyword))
+
+(defn- wire-status-name
+  [status]
+  (some-> status name))
+
+(defn- edge-claim-status-keyword
+  [value]
+  (let [status (token-keyword value)]
+    (when (contains? claims/statuses status) status)))
+
+(defn normalize-edge-claim-status
+  ([value] (normalize-edge-claim-status value :proposed))
+  ([value fallback]
+   (or (edge-claim-status-keyword value)
+       (edge-claim-status-keyword fallback)
+       :proposed)))
+
+(defn normalize-edge-claim-direction
+  [value]
+  (claims/normalize-direction (token-keyword value)))
+
+(defn- plain-scope-entry?
+  [[_ value]]
+  (and (some? value) (not (str/blank? (str value)))))
+
+(defn normalize-edge-claim-scope
+  [value]
+  (when (and (some? value)
+             (not (and (js-object? value)
+                       (let [prototype (js/Object.getPrototypeOf value)]
+                         (or (nil? prototype) (identical? prototype (.-prototype js/Object)))))))
+    (throw (ex-info "Explicit claim scope must be a plain object" {})))

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recursively reject non-JSON claim scope values**

The plain-object check applies only to the outer scope, so inputs such as `{ nested: new Date(...) }` or `{ nested: new Map(...) }` are accepted. The recursive canonicalizer treats these runtime objects as empty objects because they have no enumerable keys, causing distinct scopes to produce the same claim ID while retaining different scope values. Validate nested values as JSON primitives, arrays, or plain objects before deriving claim identity.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject colliding graph embedding owners in one ingest batch**

When two distinct events produce the same embedding node ID—for example, two `graph.node` events with the same `extra.node_id`, or an ordinary event ID matching another event's node ID—this `Map.set` silently replaces the first input. Both base events are admitted, but reconciliation then retains an embedding owned only by the later event, making the result depend on batch order and leaving the earlier source without its expected index. Detect duplicate embedding IDs with different source owners during the existing whole-batch preflight.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve partial-result diagnostics when merging quality passes**

With the default `good_then_not_bad` mode, any shortfall invokes this merge, but it propagates only unavailable partitions. If either underlying query skipped invalid-timestamp rows, its `partial: true` and `discarded_invalid_timestamp_count` are dropped; `queried_partition_count` is also lost. The high-level response can therefore report an apparently complete result even though rows were discarded, contrary to the lower-level query contract. Merge the partial flag and associated diagnostics from both passes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

+(ns openplanner.graph.claims.core
+  "Pure edge-claim domain logic.
+
+  Boundary rule: this namespace accepts only normalized CLJS data. It does not
+  inspect JavaScript objects, parse Dates, hash bytes, or defensively guess at
+  external field names. All external coercion belongs in
+  openplanner.graph.claims.boundary."
+  (:require [clojure.string :as str]))
+
+(def statuses
+  #{:proposed
+    :supported
+    :active
+    :refuted
+    :rejected
+    :superseded
+    :expired
+    :withdrawn})
+
+(def projectable-statuses #{:supported :active})
+(def directions #{:directed :undirected})
+
+(defn normalize-status
+  [status fallback]
+  (if (contains? statuses status) status fallback))
+
+(defn normalize-direction
+  [direction]
+  (if (= direction :undirected) :undirected :directed))
+
+(defn canonical-endpoints
+  [{:keys [source-node-id target-node-id direction]}]
+  (if (and (= :undirected direction)
+           (neg? (compare target-node-id source-node-id)))
+    [target-node-id source-node-id]
+    [source-node-id target-node-id]))
+
+(defn claim-id-material
+  "Returns the canonical preimage for an edge claim ID. Hashing is a boundary
+  concern so pure CLJS remains host-independent."
+  [{:keys [relation-kind direction scope-json] :as claim-key}]
+  (let [[left right] (canonical-endpoints claim-key)]
+    (str left "\n" right "\n" relation-kind "\n" (name direction) "\n" (or scope-json "{}"))))
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Encode claim ID tuples without ambiguous delimiters**

Claim identity is formed by joining unrestricted nonblank strings with newlines, so distinct endpoint tuples can have the same preimage. For example, source/target pairs `("a\nb", "c")` and `("a", "b\nc")` produce identical material when the remaining fields match, causing unrelated claims to receive the same ID and potentially overwrite one another. Encode a structured or length-prefixed tuple before hashing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-ISO legacy vector timestamps**

For stored string timestamps, `Date.parse` accepts inputs that the ingest boundary deliberately rejects, including `"2020"`, locale dates, rollover dates such as `"2021-02-30T00:00:00Z"`, and hour 24. These rows are silently converted to different timestamps and returned as valid rather than counted as discarded, producing false result metadata. Apply the same strict ISO and calendar validation used during ingest before normalizing a legacy timestamp.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
